debates.t: Contested Election for Board Chair
debates.s: Board members divided between electing incumbent Vice Chair Millicent Rogers or incumbent at-large member Joy Harrell-Goff as Board Chair immediately after four new members took their oaths.
debates.sa: Elect incumbent Vice Chair Millicent Rogers as Board Chair.
debates.sb: Elect Joy Harrell-Goff as Board Chair.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Called Meeting | 7/5/26
debates.t: Timing of Board Committee and Community Liaison Appointments
debates.s: Members debated whether to postpone all committee and liaison appointments until August onboarding or appoint standing committees immediately to support district operations.
debates.sa: Defer committee and liaison assignments until August after board onboarding and retreat.
debates.sb: Make core standing committee and liaison appointments immediately in July.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 6/25/26
debates.t: Splitting Substitute Teacher Hourly Methodology From Proposed Rate Increase
debates.s: Administration proposed simultaneously moving substitutes to hourly pay and increasing hourly rates, drawing pushback over raising substitute pay while classified staff raises remained stalled by the state budget.
debates.sa: Approve only the structural shift to hourly pay methodology now and defer substitute rate increases until fall alongside classified salary scales.
debates.sb: Original staff recommendation paired hourly methodology with $18/$19.40 hourly rate increases to strengthen substitute fill rates.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 6/25/26
debates.t: Advancing Meet and Confer Draft of Policy 1750/7220 vs Joint Legal/HR Redrafting
debates.s: Board members debated whether to honor Meet and Confer's consensus draft of employee grievance policy 1750/7220 on first read immediately or require joint legal, HR, and union redrafting first.
debates.sa: Initially proposed adopting the Meet and Confer draft on first reading and sending it to the August work session for second-read refinements.
debates.sb: Reject first-read passage until HR, board counsel, DAE/NCAE, and DAE counsel resolve operational and legal contradictions.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 6/9/26
debates.t: Allocating Coordinator/Director Raises at 3% vs 5% to Reallocate $263k to Lower Wage Grades
debates.s: During the budget update, board members debated whether to cap coordinator and director salary increases at 3% instead of 5% so roughly $263,000 could be shifted to lower-paid classified staff.
debates.sa: Stress-test reducing coordinator/director raises from 5% to 3% to free $263,000 for lower-paid workers.
debates.sb: Preserve uniform scale adjustments and avoid worsening salary compression among mid-level administrators.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 6/9/26
debates.t: Immediate Authorization of Right-Sizing Consultant vs Reviewing Draft RFP First
debates.s: Administration asked for early green-light support to hire a third-party right-sizing and consolidation consultant, while board members demanded to review a concrete RFP and board-engagement plan first.
debates.sa: Require staff to bring a draft RFP with scope, optional plan, budget, and board engagement timeline before authorizing procurement.
debates.sb: Seek early board backing to accelerate third-party facility utilization planning ahead of future bond cycles.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 6/9/26
debates.t: Adding 'Briefly' Modifier to Policy 4326 Section A3b on Calming/Comforting Students
debates.s: Board members split 6-1 over adding the word 'briefly' to define permissible physical calming/comforting exceptions in Policy 4326 on seclusion and restraint.
debates.sa: Insert 'briefly' before 'calm or comfort' to prevent prolonged physical holds from being misclassified.
debates.sb: Omit 'briefly' to avoid putting caring educators at vague disciplinary risk while comforting distressed children.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 6/9/26
debates.t: PreK-5 Level 1B Out-of-School Suspensions and EC Principal Supervisor Review (Policy 4301.1)
debates.s: Members debated prohibiting Level 1B suspensions across PreK-5 and requiring principal supervisor review for all PreK-5 suspensions of students with disabilities.
debates.sa: Expand oversight to require principal supervisor review before suspending any PreK-5 student with a disability and curb Level 1B exclusions.
debates.sb: Retain administrative discretion for escalating safety disruptions and avoid overextending supervisor review beyond PreK-2 capacity.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 6/9/26
debates.t: Policy 4301 'Must' vs 'May' IEP/504 Compliance Language
debates.s: Following legal counsel advice, the board voted 6-1 to soften 'must' to 'may' and remove a trailing legal compliance sentence in Policy 4301 regarding IEP/504 reviews.
debates.sa: Adopt counsel's edit from 'must' to 'may' and trim redundant statutory compliance language from the handbook matrix.
debates.sb: Preserve mandatory 'must' language inside Policy 4301 so school staff see binding disability protections directly in the Code of Conduct.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 5/28/26
debates.t: Scheduling Second Reading of Policy 8600 (Work Session vs Monthly Meeting)
debates.s: Board members disagreed briefly over whether to waive work-session rules to adopt Policy 8600 on second reading at the June 9 work session or hold final action for the June 25 regular monthly meeting.
debates.sa: Bring Policy 8600 back to the June 9 work session (with a policy waiver if needed) to avoid delay.
debates.sb: Send Policy 8600 to the June 25 regular monthly meeting without waiving the work-session discussion policy.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 5/14/26
debates.t: Bypassing Policy Committee Tier Queue (Policy 2231) to Discuss Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer)
debates.s: The board split sharply over whether two board members could use Policy 2330 agenda rules to bring proposed Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer) edits directly to the board table without going through Policy 2231's prioritized tiering queue.
debates.sa: Permit two board members to place Policy 7215 discussion on the work session agenda and clarify conflicts with Policy 2231 prior to May 31 certification.
debates.sb: Enforce Policy 2231 strictly so Policy 7215 cannot jump ahead of 30 tiered policies already voted on by the full board.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 5/14/26
debates.t: Extent of PreK-5 Suspension Prohibitions and Staffing Support Under Policy 4301
debates.s: Members agreed on expanding restorative practices in Policy 4301 but differed on whether to ban Level 1B/all suspensions up through Grade 3 or Grade 5 immediately given budget and staffing cuts.
debates.sa: Prohibit Level 1B suspensions (disrespect/non-compliance) for young students, include PreK-3 explicitly, and expand supervisor/EC checks across K-5.
debates.sb: Start with PreK-2 limits, preserve principal/supervisor discretion for serious safety issues, and ensure staff capacity before banning higher grades.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 4/23/26
debates.t: Legislative Priorities Framing on School Vouchers and Charter Expansion
debates.s: Board members debated how forcefully to frame opposition to private school vouchers and charter school expansion while maintaining coalition appeal with rural North Carolina school districts.
debates.sa: Use 'school vouchers' instead of 'opportunity scholarships', standardize behind a full moratorium, and avoid wording implying support for charter expansion.
debates.sb: Use statutory/NCSBA terminology ('opportunity scholarships', pause/phase-out, accountability & transparency) to maximize coalition reach with rural boards.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 4/23/26
debates.t: Policy 5120 Federal Immigration Enforcement Entry & Main-Office Protocol (F1 & F2)
debates.s: Members and district safety leadership debated whether Policy 5120 Section F1 should remove 'report to the school's main office' and instruct principals to ask unannounced immigration officers to wait outside or in the main office.
debates.sa: Remove 'report to the school's main office' from F1 so policy clearly expects contact with the Superintendent's office first, and require principals in F2 to as
debates.sb: Preserve practical main-office containment without putting unarmed school principals in confrontational standoffs telling federal agents to leave.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 4/9/26
debates.t: International Teacher J-1 to H-1B Visa Renewal Policy and Retention Exemptions
debates.s: Following public outcry over Murray Massenberg art teacher Elvin Herrera, board members questioned administration's refusal to pursue H-1B visa transitions for J-1 international teachers.
debates.sa: Question why pandemic-era H-1B exceptions ended without board notice and explore retention pathways for exemplary international teachers.
debates.sb: Standard practice always limited J-1 cultural exchange contracts to 3+2 years with mandatory two-year home residency, and pandemic H-1Bs were strictly temporary

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 4/9/26
debates.t: Secondary Magnet Express Bus Stops: Immediate 2027-28 Commitment vs 2026-27 Pilot Only
debates.s: Board members split over whether to give conditional approval now to roll out express bus stops to all secondary magnets in 2027-28 (to give lottery families notice) or limit direction strictly to the 2026-27 pilot at DSA and Brogden DLI.
debates.sa: Approve planning for Phase 2 expansion to all secondary magnets in 2027-28 now (subject to later rollback if needed) so families know before magnet lotteries.
debates.sb: Separate out the 2026-27 pilot (DSA and Brogden DLI) and withhold any commitment on other secondary magnets until Q1 data is reviewed by the incoming board.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 3/26/26
debates.t: Flat 12.08% vs Graduated Classified Pay Scale Raise Distribution
debates.s: Board members disagreed philosophically over applying a flat 12.08% raise across all classified steps versus graduating percentages downward for senior central administrators.
debates.sa: Explore a graduated raise model awarding 12% to lower-paid staff and smaller percentages at the coordinator-and-above tiers.
debates.sb: Maintain uniform 12.08% modeling in the county request to avoid pay compression and protect upward career incentives.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 3/26/26
debates.t: Capital Technology Lease ($2.82M Chromebooks & Interactive Displays) vs Facilities/Screen-Time Concerns
debates.s: Public commenters and several board members questioned prioritizing $2.82M in leased Chromebooks and BrightLink replacements over HVAC repairs and screen-time limits.
debates.sa: Scrutinize $2.8M technology spending relative to HVAC repairs, teacher pay, and childhood screen-time risks.
debates.sb: Fund multi-year leases to replace failing 13-year-old projectors and out-of-warranty Chromebooks to prevent instructional disruption and digital inequity.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 3/12/26
debates.t: Including Extra Duty Pay Increases and 3% Central Office Reductions in FY 2026-27 Budget Draft
debates.s: Board members divided over whether to add an Extra Duty Pay increase (potentially funded via 3% Central Office cuts) into the Phase 2 budget proposal now or resolve school-level stipend inequities and payroll/comp-time compliance first.
debates.sa: Include extra duty pay increases in the FY 2026-27 budget ask immediately to recognize specialists, coaches, and staff working beyond contract hours.
debates.sb: Audit and standardize school-level stipend administration, payroll lines, and comp-time rules before committing recurring new dollars.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 3/12/26
debates.t: Policy 5120 Scope on Immigration Enforcement, Judicial Warrants, and Exigent Circumstances
debates.s: Members and public speakers scrutinized whether draft Policy 5120 clearly assigns decision-making to principals, differentiates federal immigration officers from local law enforcement, and avoids overly broad 'exigent circumstances' exceptions.
debates.sa: Tighten wording on principal authority, judicial warrant checks, and immigration enforcement definitions before final adoption.
debates.sb: Advance the committee's current draft through First Read now while addressing remaining wording refinements in Policy Committee.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Budget Hearing | 3/5/26
debates.t: Classified Wage Levels, Custodian Overtime/80-Hour Caps, and OT/PT Assistant Inclusion Amid County Revenue Limits
debates.s: While no split votes occurred during the public hearing, speakers and board members surfaced a sharp policy tension between employee demands for comprehensive classified pay, custodial workload reform, and COTA/PTA inclusion versus Durham County's warning of constrained tax capacity.
debates.sa: Substantially exceed a 5% baseline raise by eliminating custodian 80-hour caps/unpaid overtime, including OT/PT assistants in salary realignment, and matching c
debates.sb: Balance classified compensation priorities against Durham County's tight fiscal outlook, continuation cost pressures, and competing capital/HVAC needs.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 2/26/26
debates.t: 50% Flat After-School Tuition Increase vs. Lower/Phased Rate and Expanded Low-Income Discounts
debates.s: Board members split 5-2 over adopting administration's recommended 50% flat tuition hike while maintaining current financial assistance versus adopting a gentler 40% increase or pairing the 50% rate with a 50% discount for low-income families.

debates.sb: Soften the immediate financial shock on working families via a 40% phased increase or a 50% discount offset by higher-income contributions.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 2/26/26

debates.sa: Prioritize Seclusion & Restraint (1st) and Child Abuse Reporting (2nd), followed by Budget Transparency (3rd) and Student Code of Conduct (4th).
debates.sb: Place Student Code of Conduct ahead of Budget Transparency so restorative discipline matrices can be finalized before summer handbook printing.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 2/9/26
debates.t: $4.6M/Year Student Device Model, Screen-Time Guardrails, and Work Session Action Authority
debates.s: Board members differed sharply over the urgency and cost of a $23M five-year student device refresh, leading to a unanimous roll-call vote to table the plan for stronger academic and screen-time guardrails.
debates.sa: Delay approval pending instructional evidence, screen-time limits, cost reductions, and compliance with Policy 2235.
debates.sb: Treat student devices as essential academic and testing infrastructure requiring predictable refresh funding.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 2/9/26
debates.t: Structure and Cost of DAE Meet & Confer Classified Pay Proposal ($29.5M)
debates.s: During the budget update, CFO Jeremy Teter and Board member Natalie Beyer challenged the equity and fiscal structure of DAE's $22/hr plus 0.75% step proposal estimated at $29.5M.
debates.sa: Critique DAE's $22/hr proposal excluding administrators as fiscally unsustainable and inequitable in structure.
debates.sb: Continue exploring aggressive classified wage scenarios that lift lowest-paid workers and address compression for future simulator iterations.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 1/29/26
debates.t: Delaying After-School Fee Decision to Build Sliding-Scale Tuition Models vs. Preserving Camp Registration Timelines
debates.s: The Board divided 4-3 over directing administration to spend four weeks building sliding-scale tuition models comparable in revenue to a 50% hike, knowing it would push summer camp registration from February 16 into March.
debates.sa: Require sliding-scale tuition models by February 26 before raising rates so higher-income families can offset lower-income increases.
debates.sb: Avoid delaying summer camp and after-school registration timelines or imposing sliding-scale modeling without reliable family income data.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 1/15/26
debates.t: Discipline Data Gaps, Pre-K Suspensions, and Falling Panorama Survey Participation
debates.s: While administration highlighted a 29%-30% drop in overall discipline incidents, public commenters and board scrutiny surfaced unresolved gaps in Pre-K suspension tracking, opt-in survey decline (90% to 60%), and EC restorative implementation.
debates.sa: Address gaps in Pre-K suspension data tracking, restore Panorama student/family survey participation, and verify restorative compliance.
debates.sb: Build on the 29% year-over-year and 30% first-quarter incident reductions through continued RPC/STS support and Code of Conduct implementation.

debates.mt: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 12/11/25
